# Spark Control Center 1.2.4

This patch makes job reuse clearer and lets alert rules cover specific diagnostic failures.

## Reusable YAML templates

- Clone, retry, and template-save operations remove runtime status, Kubernetes managed metadata, finalizers/owner references, the previous submitter, and `kubectl.kubernetes.io/last-applied-configuration`.
- Templates are edited and saved as compact YAML. Existing JSON manifests are normalized when edited, copied, or rendered; historical version snapshots remain unchanged.
- Parameter definitions now use a form with names, types, defaults, allowed values, regex validation, and descriptions.
- Typed parameters remain integers/numbers/booleans in the rendered YAML, and string values cannot inject extra YAML fields. Kubernetes dry-run remains mandatory for submission.

## Diagnostic alerts

- New diagnostic-fingerprint rules can select `VOLUME_MOUNT`, `APPLICATION_FAILED`, image pull, scheduling, OOM, Executor loss, RBAC, observed codes, or future codes entered manually.
- Leave codes empty to match all current and future diagnoses. Concurrent codes produce independent alerts with evidence and recommendations.
- Fingerprint cards have a shortcut for creating a rule, and the evaluator includes Kubernetes events for event-only failures such as `FailedMount`.
- Existing alert types, namespace authorization, Webhooks, and immutable rule versions remain compatible. PostgreSQL adds `diagnostic_codes` automatically during startup.

See the [template and alert guide](https://github.com/ApolloMeridian/spark-application-webui/blob/v1.2.4/docs/TEMPLATES-AND-ALERTS.md).

## Release assets

- `spark-control-center-1.2.4.tar`
- `spark-control-center-backend-1.2.4.tar`
- `spark-control-center-1.2.4.tgz`
- `SHA256SUMS`

Images are tagged `spark-control-center:1.2.4` and `spark-control-center-backend:1.2.4`, without a private registry prefix. Load the image tar files with `docker load`, then upgrade the Helm release using your local production values. Existing database data and rule/template history are preserved.
